item.description:
Kento Alpha 0.8, build 1656

A plane drawn on the plate

  • A Projection can go onto a plane you draw over the picture: choose a plane drawn on the plate in the onto menu (or Draw a plane on the plate in the Viewer's menu), click its four corners at the hold frame, and give it a depth from a tracked point or a typed one. A perspective grid and its size show while the corners can be a rectangle; when they can't, the hint says why.
  • Drag a corner to refine it, one undo a drag. The plane is a Card beside the Projection whose lattice holds the corners exactly, so a Nuke script shows the same plane.
  • On a still with no camera, Camera from this plane makes one from the drawing.

3D renders

  • Geometry running under or behind the camera, a floor or a road toward the lens, now renders up to the frame's edge instead of dropping out.
  • Objects with a BlendMat or MergeMat that pass through each other are now in front where they are nearer, at each pixel.
  • Card2's deformation lattice (bilinear and bicubic) renders as in Nuke scripts that use it.
  • A scene with more than 16 surfaces now draws copies of one object together and says when anything is left out.

Remote control

  • Preferences > Performance > Remote control lets scripts, pipeline tools and assistants that speak MCP drive the open comp: describe it, make, wire and change nodes, render a frame, read pixels, save, undo. Local only, behind a token; each change is one undo, marked in History.

Faster

  • Rotated, skewed or scaled Transforms render about twice as fast, with the same picture to the bit.
  • The median( values, count ) of pixel kernels now runs on the graphics card too.

More

  • A World-space blur pixel kernel, usable now that kernels run on the graphics card.
  • Nuke scripts: expressions written as [value knob] (as the CameraShake2 gizmo's centre is) are read, and ChannelMerge's older intersect operation is read as in.

Kento Alpha 0.8, build 1631

Pixel kernels on the GPU

  • PixelKernels run on the graphics card: an HD frame of a heavy kernel in hundredths of a second where the processor took seconds (Painterly 2.7 s to 0.01 s; the anisotropic Kuwahara from our comps, 58 s to under a quarter of a second). The pictures are the processor's, exactly or to a few millionths.
  • GPU on the Kernel tab and in the kernel's window switches it for one node, and beside it Kento says where the kernel runs and why. A script keeps the switch as its node's own setting.
  • Preferences > Performance > Processing, GPU, nodes that support it, now covers pixel kernels too.

Faster

  • Writing EXRs uses every core: an HD frame read and written in 0.027 s instead of 0.089, as fast as other compositing apps; renders of Grade, Blur and Merge comps are two to three times faster.

More ready-made kernels

  • Antialiasing recovery, Rank filter, Texture tile, Line drawer and Recursive warp vectors, by their authors' permission; S-curve (with its exact inverse) and Quantize. Their authors are credited in About.
  • The kernel language gains median( values, count ).
  • Kernels you save or export are .pk files; Import still reads the kernel files of other tools.

Fixed

  • A kernel whose init() sets its controls could read freed memory as it compiled, and crash.
  • Installed OpenFX plugins are told Kento is an image effect host, as the newest OpenFX asks.

Kento Alpha 0.8, build 1613

Installed plugins

  • LensNode loads and renders (on the GPU). Its menus use a newer kind of plugin control that Kento now reads.
  • A plugin's panel is laid out as the plugin lays it out: its groups fold as sections of one tab, and its buttons sit where it puts them. Each change is passed to the plugin, so menus it fills (LensNode's Family and Variant after Manufacturer) and controls it hides or dims follow.
  • A plugin's own window (Neat Video's Prepare Profile) opens from its button, and what it sets there comes back to the node as one undo.
  • Plugins that can't render part of a frame are given the whole frame: Neat Video denoises correctly.

Pixel kernels

  • Ten ready-made kernels under Nodes > Other > Pixel kernels, each with its own controls: Fix bad pixels, Firefly killer, Normals from height, Ambient occlusion from depth, Alpha stroke, Painterly (Kuwahara), Curvature from normals, STMap extension, Triplanar texture and Panini projection. A kernel menu on the panel swaps between them; their authors are credited in About.
  • Writing a kernel: the code is colored, its lines numbered, and the error's line marked with the wrong word underlined in red. Names are offered as you type; Return keeps the indent, Cmd-/ comments, Cmd-D duplicates, Cmd-L goes to a line, brackets match. The kernel applies a moment after you stop typing.
  • The kernel in its own window, resizable and full screen, with find and replace and the language's reference beside the code. Save to library keeps your kernels with versions; Export and Import write and read .blink files; a studio's shared folder can be set in Preferences.

Send to paint

  • Soft, half-transparent strokes from a paint app come back as painted. A painting reloads after a save in the paint app as soon as its comp is open.

Fixed

  • Undoing a change to a pixel kernel's code works again.
